en: Oṃ, homage to Mahābhairava; Oṃ, homage to Kubjikā.
Homage to you, the Great Śāna, the supreme lord who acts according to his own will.
And it is joined with Kubjikā and adorned with supreme bliss.
Proclaimed by Bhairava and Bhairavī, she has arrived at the dissolution into the supreme reality.
The *Dīkṣāsārottara* is the essence of essences, which severs the suffering of men.
The fifth is the initiation of the covenant (samayadīkṣā), and the second is that of Vasiṣṭha.
The third is the supreme sequence of initiation for the benefit of humanity, which is the universal authority of Nirvāṇa through the initiation of differentiation.
It removes the sins accumulated over seven lifetimes and bestows immortality.
It increases longevity, glory, beauty, good fortune, prosperity, and nourishment.
By means of the eight vowels, one attains the power of moving through the sky; by the mere sight of them, sins are destroyed.
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hsphraṃ Hsauṃ, the sandals for the venerable Guru and the Vīrayonis. (5)
First, one should perform worship to Gaṇeśa for the sake of removing obstacles and accomplishing one's desired aim.
Likewise, one should perform the worship for the sake of unimpeded accomplishment upon the seat of the woodpecker.
Thereafter, with the preceptor at the head and the others, one should prepare a square mandala;
likewise, in front of the seat of knowledge (vidyāpīṭha), there should be a mandala in the shape of a mandala.
(5) From the sandals of the venerable Guru, [I offer] this sandal. (5) Thus ends the lineage of purification. [Name of the person, etc. (5).
"Of the one whose mandala is unbroken," and so forth. Thus, having performed the honor to the Guru.
(5) Kini (2) Vicce Konāyai Hraḥ Phaṭ, [this is] for the Astra-mantra; [I offer] the sandals. (5) ||
Having sprinkled water mixed with sandalwood, unbroken rice grains, and flowers upon the Guru, one should construct a mandala.
The earth has been filled with the essence of Madhu and Kaiṭabha;
having empowered the medicinal herbs, I sprinkle them with fragrant water.
The earth was purified and the white waters were made to flow.
O noble one, the evil, good, and bad deeds committed in previous births [bear fruit].
Having joined the palms at the back of the head, one should mentally revolve [the mantra] here for sins committed in this life and in other lives.
By offering a stream of unbroken *mālā* flowers with humility before the Guru,
various kinds of flowers are born into various lineages.
O Protector, may they all be patient with me; may you always protect me.
(5) Regarding the *Śrīsaṃvarttāmaṇḍala* and so forth: by means of this mantra, one should smear the mandala.
One should draw a square mandala measuring one cubit with colored powders upon the body of the Guru-Snake.
The worship at the nostril-gate: "A, homage to Anantālā. With this mantra, one should place a flower in the center of the maṇḍala.

(5) "Aiṃ hūṃ phaṭ, in the vajra-penetrating cage. One should hold the flower with the left hand. "Lāhile calamakule kulamacale hrīṃ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā. With this mantra, [one places it] in the center of the maṇḍala.
Sleep the flower. Worship it. In the center, worship [the deity] ending with the *ahaṃkāra* of Navātman using the *kuta* mantra.
(5) Ha 9 Sa 9 Pādukā. In the center.
(5) Homage to the Blessed One, the digit of the heart; *hrā*, homage to the heart, the pervader of the earth, in the east.
HSPHEṂ, to Kujikā, the lamp of the lineage, HRĪṂ ŚRĪṂ, obeisance to the head, ĀPATATVĀYE. [To be placed] on the right.
(5) Hrāṃ hrīṃ hūṃ, to the crest of tawny hair, hūṃ; obeisance to the crest, the element of fire, in the north.
O Ghora, Aghora, Ghorāmukhī, Bahurūpā! Hreṃ Śrīṃ! Homage to the armor, to the wind element.
In the west: (5) Chāṃ chīṃ, homage to Mahantārikā; hrīṃ śrīṃ, homage to the eyes; homage to the principle of space (ākāśatattva).
In the center: (5) KINI (2) VICCE KROKANĀYE HRAṂ ASTĀYA SARVATATTVĀYA NAMAḤ. From the southeast to the northeast. Again, worship in the inner maṇḍala.
(5) Homage to the Blessed Lady Śrī-Urddhavaktrā; [place] the sandals in the center. (5) |||
(5) HSKHPHRAṂ, the sandals for the eastern face. (5) ||
(5) Hrāṃ hrīṃ hraṃ, the sandals of the glorious southern face; [to] the south.
(5) O Ghore, Aghore, Aghorāmukhī! [I worship] the sandal-paste (pādukā) at the venerable northern face in the north. (5) In the north.
(5) Chāṃ chiṃ, to Mahantārikā at the glorious western face: Pā pādukāṃ. (5) In the west.
(5) Kini (2) Vicce, to the mouth of Krokanā, the Śrīparāparā, [I offer] the sandals; in the center.
(5) Homage to the solar mandala. (5) Homage to the fierce mandala. (5) Homage to the fire mandala.

(5) Salutations to Akhaṇḍamaṇḍalā! [I offer] sandalwood paste, unbroken rice, flowers, vermilion, fruit, betel leaf, grains of rice, incense, lamps, food offerings, along with wine and bali-offerings, together with self-satisfaction, and so forth. May she, being well-pleased, grant boons. [Stotra:]
Salutations to that glorious Guru, whose form is the shape of an unbroken circle, by whom the moving and the unmoving are pervaded, and who bestows the state of liberation. 1.
For one whose vision is obscured by the cataract of ignorance, with the salve-stick of knowledge—
Salutation to that glorious Guru by whom the eye was opened. || 2 ||
I salute the Guru, who is like Śiva himself—mounted upon the power of knowledge, adorned with the garland of principles (tattvas), and the bestower of both worldly enjoyment and liberation. 3.
The Guru is Brahmā, the Guru is Viṣṇu, and the Guru is the divine Maheśvara.
The entire world is the Guru-deity; salutations to that illustrious Guru. 4.
To the Guru who is most venerable, and to those others who are like brothers to the Guru, through the grace of the Guru’s consort, I bow to the Guru as Śiva himself. 5.
To the giver of the path to liberation, the cutter of the bonds of saṃsāra.
I bow down to the glorious Guru, who is the beginning, the first of beginnings, and without beginning.
He is the action, the meditation, and the Dharma, the awakener of the path to initiation.
To him who is the awakening of both ignorance and knowledge, [I bow] to that venerable Guru, the deity.
The giver of the supreme syllable, who has reached the further shore by cutting through cyclic existence.
May the giver be one who crosses over the difficult; salutations to that glorious Guru. || 8 ||
The sacred site is the deity, the mother is the deity, and the guru is the supreme deity.
The world is blissful in form; forgive me, salutation to the Guru. || 9 ||
O four-faced one, four-armed, yellow-bodied, and clad in yellow garments, you who hold the rosary and the book—salutations to your feet, O Guru. (10)
O Guru, for you who are the King of Gurus, that [state] is difficult to attain even for a guru.
And through the grace of the Guru’s word, purification of the physical body (piṇḍa) arises. || 11 ||
The sin committed over seven lifetimes is cleared away, and one is freed from all diseases;
whether a Brahmin, a Kshatriya, or a Chandala, they follow this single path. || 12 ||
The mouth of the Guru's feet is the Gaṅgā; the form of the Guru is the goddess Sarasvatī.
In Kāśī, the word of the Guru is Śiva; the word of the Guru is the supreme state. || 13 ||
Herein are the perfumes and so forth. [Thus ends the *Śrī-Gaṅgādharapaṭṭa-gurustava*.]

For the offering of *argha* to the Guru, recite the *Gurumaṇḍalastotra*. Recite the various verses beginning with "ruji. (12) Offer *argha* with conch shells and camphor. [Recite] the names of the Guru, the month, the lunar mansion (*nakṣatra*), and so forth. (5) O Goddess of the gods, for the sake of fulfillment, accept this *argha* offered by me; be gracious to the Guru.

Salutation! Salutation to the feet of the Guru, the source of initiation! With a mind [intent on] the sacred thread (*yajñopavīta*), and with offerings of fruit and food (*naivedya*) mixed with honey and sugar, I offer this to you, the venerable Guru, who has been fully worshipped and who bestows the state of the Great Swan (*mahāhaṃsa*). Having previously offered [these], the face of the Guru is seen by means of the crest-lock (*śikhā*). [This is done with] a handful of flowers (*puṣpāñjali*).

One should recite: "Terrified by the fear of saṃsāra, I have come for refuge to the Teaching. I am unable to endure the suffering of birth, death, old age, and so forth; therefore, through body, mind, and speech, I confess my misdeeds."
May there be favor for me, and may whatever obstacles there may be be overcome by the month-observers.
If the validity of a means of knowledge, such as direct perception and so forth, were to depend upon verbal testimony;
If the command of my guru should become manifest before you.
May he uproot this flood of snares that has cut me down from my narrow path;
having understood this terrible state, I have no other refuge but him.
Therefore, O Lord, out of compassion, grant me the bestowal of initiation;
for when knowledge is given along with its true nature, the latent impressions of karma are destroyed.
Therefore, out of compassion for me, grant me the measure of initiation.
Having spoken thus, [he should offer] with a prostration of the staff; this is the threefold offering of flowers.
In the midst of the Javana Mandara ocean, having paid homage to the Guru, [one recites]: *Oṃ kāyaśuddhi namaḥ*.

Having paid homage to the Guru, may there be refuge. *Oṃ vākśuddhi namaḥ*. Having paid homage to the Guru, may there be refuge. Again: *Cittaśuddhi namaḥ*. Having paid homage to the Guru, may there be refuge. Again: Body, Speech, and Mind.
Salutations to You alone, the Self of all. By the Guru: "May You be my refuge; may You destroy my prostrations."
Praise of Forbearance: You are the refuge of all beings; I have not recited [your name]. Standing once more and having prostrated, [I offer this praise].
The sacrificial fee is the entirety; it is the time of the Mandara [offering].
Hymn of Praise.
Homage to you, Maṇḍarāja, and to you, the sovereign of all principles; homage be to you, the Maṇḍala that illuminates the earth, the atmosphere, and the heavens.
I must perform the ritual actions for the sake of my own success.
Forgiveness is appropriate for a teacher who is pleased by his disciple; therefore, let there be salutation to this teacher.
Thus concludes the dismissal of the maṇḍala. [The mantra: *madalasaṣoṅa svānagvayugvāla*. The teacher receives the sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*).
When the day was auspicious, under the asterism of Hari (Śravaṇā), and his mind was perfectly serene.
"O Lord, you are willing to grant me that supreme gift of initiation;
O son, I shall grant it to you with this well-pleased splendor."

"By the grace of the Guru's feet, by the favor of Īśvara—may it be so! Having accepted this, [performs] the dismissal of the maṇḍala. [He offers] the great *ālambuṣā* [stalk] into the middle of the *sindhalaka* [vessel].
Victory to the Guru! May the reality of the Self, Knowledge, and Śiva be for our great prosperity. [Offering] all flowers, one performs prostration at the head.
Having offered the *nirmālya* flower to Īśāna, one worships the *nirmālya* flower with:
"Oṃ, obeisance to Caṇḍa, the recipient of the *nirmālya*. One washes the hands. [Thus ends the ritual procedure for the worship of the Guru-maṇḍala.]

Then, having performed the purification of the elements (*bhūtaśuddhi*), breath control (*prāṇāyāma*), and the placement of the letters (*mātṛkānyāsa*) starting from the feet, one should avoid the sin of killing a Brahmin, the sin of approaching a forbidden woman, and the sin of killing a cow for four ages, as declared by the gods in the mantras. One should avoid the *laula* and *maṃnala* [impurities] and proceed with the rite of cessation (*nivartana*). Having offered the *svadhā* libation at the crest, [one performs] the purification of the elements and breath control. [Then follows] the *mātṛkānyāsa* from the feet upward.
One should meditate on the region from the knees downward as the seat of Earth (pṛthivī), which is square and yellow in color, presided over by the deity Brahmā;
in its center, one should contemplate the seed-syllable *la*. From the knees upward to the navel is the seat of Water (āpas), shaped like a bow.

One should meditate on the white-colored [syllable] whose deity is Viṣṇu, and within that, the seed-syllable. From the navel up to the heart, one should meditate on the locus of radiance, which is triangular in shape, dark blue in color, and contains the seed-syllable in its center. From the heart up to the throat...

The locus of air (vāyu) is hexagonal in shape, black in color, with Maheśvara as its presiding deity; one should meditate on the seed-syllable *yaṃ* in its center. From the throat up to the forehead is the locus of space (ākāśa), which is square in shape, smoke-colored, with Sadāśiva as its presiding deity; the seed-syllable *haṃ* is meditated upon in its center.
Six syllables per foot; sixty-two [syllables] here; [this is] the *nasvardhana* [meter].
In the section on the element of earth, one should place the sandals at the location of the crest-lock (śikhā).
In the section concerning the descent [of power], one should place the pādukā in the location of the bindu.
In the section concerning the element of fire, [one should meditate upon] the Heart Sandal.
During the period of the air element, one should place the sandals at the location of the navel.
At the time of the reality of space, [place] the sandal upon the secret place.
At the time of the authority over the Brahman-principle, [one should place] the knees, heart, and feet [in their respective positions].
In the section on the reality of Viṣṇu, [he gave] the sandals for two quarters.
In the section concerning the principle of Rudra, there is a pair of sandals for the two hands.
One should increase by one at each of the eight positions.

(5) In the section on the Śiva-tattva: *śauṃ*, the *pādukā* for the head, addressed to the Supreme (*parā*). (5) In the section on the Ātman-tattva: *hrīṃ hrīṃ hūṃ śauṃ phaṭ*, the *pādukā* for the heart, addressed to the Non-Supreme (*aparā*). *aghore hrīṃ paramaghore hruṃ ghorarūpe hraṃ ghorāmukhī*.

*O Bhīmabhīṣaṇe, blow! (2) Drink! (2) Ruru! Phaṭ! Hsauṃ! Huṃ! Phaṭ!* To the secret sandals (*pādukā*) belonging to the higher and lower [levels] within the domain of the *vidyā-tattva*, obeisance! To the *pṛthivī-tattva*, obeisance! At the foundation (*ādhāra*), obeisance to the *āpa-tattva*!

*Teja-tattvāya namaḥ* at the navel; (5) *Vāyu-tattvāya namaḥ* at the heart; (5) *Āpa-tattvāya namaḥ* at the throat; (5) *Brahma-tattvāya namaḥ* at the knees; *Viṣṇu-tattvāya namaḥ* at the feet; (5) *Rudra-tattvāya namaḥ* at the hands. With these [mantras], purify the eight locations. Then, [offer] a handful of flowers (*puṣpāñjali*) with the hands.

Perform the ritual slaughter (*vadhālaya*). Worship the goddesses of one's own horses (*svaśvadevī*). Offer three *añjali* salutations. [Recite] the *Chāyā*. [Recite] the *Ṣaḍagati* and so forth. Offer incense (*dhūpa*) and lamps (*dīpa*).
Offer the food oblation (*naivedya*). Perform the recitation (*japa*) ten times. Recite the hymn (*stotra*). [Recite] the *Akhaṇḍamaṇḍalā* and so forth.
"Mayā-kuṇḍala-nitya," etc.; "tapaṇa"; "sama-yacchāya"; "dakṣiṇāyāya"; "ekāneka," etc.; "visarjjanayāṅgāva."
With a hundred skull-bowls || [which are] like mere dreams || Oṃ hrīṃ li (2) to the wielder of the trident || svāhā ||

In the year 801, on the ninth day of the bright fortnight of the month of Jyeṣṭha, the auspicious Śrī Haripati Deva, the son of Coyaāju, performed this meritorious act for the sake of his parents. May it be auspicious.
Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ śrīcintāmaṇe svāhā.

Oṃ! To the one who teaches the land of Kāmarūpa; to the goddess Tāhāvathe; to the yoginīs of Annadi; to those who have gone to the path of the noose (pāśa); to those who have come from Kādi; to those who have come from Latālona; to those who have come from Mithikhāna; to those who have come from Gāyika; to the queen of Vācchā; to the queen of Puruka; to those who have come from Bhaiśāka; to those who have come from Vādāka; [this is] the mantra for the seat of Sarijā.
